lines.tts: The game master just agreed to lower my difficulty...
From the M L H Solana Hackathon, this is Oath-roll!
You're Wren, stealing a silver bell clapper. You get five turns to fill the progress bar. Each turn, type whatever you try.
The Keeper, an AI game master, answers with a D C, the number you need on a d20, and what happens on each result. Then it's sealed on Solana.
Before you roll, you can plead for an easier D C. Plain demands get you nowhere.
Flattery, though? He agrees to fourteen.
He really sends that change to Solana, with your words in it. And the program refuses. Table Sealed. The D C stays at sixteen.
Now roll. The number comes from Magic Block's verifiable randomness, right on chain.
Every roll gets a proof page. Your browser checks on Solana that the ruling was sealed before the roll, and that the dice came from the V R F.
Fill the bar before the tide comes back, and the clapper is yours.
And every plea Solana refused ends up here, on the Wall of Refused Pleas.
Oath-roll. Running on Solana devnet, with the code and every transaction on GitHub.
